items.stem: Which Kubernetes object provides a stable address and load-balances traffic to a changing set of Pods?

options.rationale: Correct: a Service gives a stable virtual IP and DNS name in front of Pods matched by a selector.
A Pod's IP is ephemeral and changes on restart.
A ConfigMap stores configuration, not networking.
A Namespace is an isolation boundary, not a load balancer.

items.explanation: Correct: a Service gives a stable virtual IP and DNS name in front of Pods matched by a selector.

items.stem: What is the purpose of a readiness probe?

options.text: To tell Kubernetes when a Pod is ready to receive traffic
options.rationale: Correct: readiness probes gate traffic until the container reports ready.

options.text: To restart a container that has crashed
options.rationale: That is the liveness probe's role.

options.text: To set CPU and memory limits
options.rationale: Limits are set in the resources field, not by probes.

options.text: To scale the Deployment up and down
options.rationale: Scaling is handled by replicas or an autoscaler.

items.explanation: Correct: readiness probes gate traffic until the container reports ready.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Kubernetes Deployments are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets to keep a desired number of Pods running
options.rationale: Correct: Deployments reconcile the actual Pod count toward the declared replicas.

options.text: A rolling update can be rolled back to a previous revision
Deleting a Pod managed by a Deployment permanently reduces capacity
options.rationale: The controller recreates the Pod to match the desired count.

options.text: A Deployment stores persistent application data by itself
options.rationale: Persistent data needs volumes and PersistentVolumeClaims.

items.explanation: Correct: Deployments reconcile the actual Pod count toward the declared replicas.; Correct: Deployment revisions support rollback.
